w:r.w:t: RMG Worker Safety & Digital Production Tracking Platform
Architecture foundation reused from the LAUNDRIX project
Prepared for: NITER Innovate Hackathon 2026 — RMG Industry Track

is a digital platform designed to solve two connected, real problems in Bangladesh's Ready-Made Garments (RMG) industry: (1) workers have no safe, trackable way to report safety hazards or grievances, and (2) factories track production (cutting → sewing → QC → packing) manually, with no real-time visibility into where a batch of garments currently is or whether it passed quality checks.
Instead of building two disconnected tools,

unifies both under one role-based platform: workers and line supervisors interact with the same bundle/QR system that quality inspectors use for compliance checks, and the same platform lets any worker anonymously raise a grievance that HR can track to resolution — all inside one factory-operations dashboard.

The system deliberately reuses the architecture, data-modeling patterns, and workflow logic already designed and validated in the LAUNDRIX project (a Multi-Branch & Multi-Vendor Laundry Management Platform), because LAUNDRIX already solved the same core technical problem: tracking a physical item through a multi-stage process using QR/barcode scans, batching items together, running quality inspection on them, and giving different roles different dashboards over the same data.

To give every RMG worker a safe channel to be heard, and every factory floor a simple digital system to know exactly where production stands — without requiring expensive hardware or enterprise software budgets.

To become the standard lightweight operations layer for small-and-mid-sized RMG factories in Bangladesh — starting with worker safety and bundle tracking, and expanding toward the fuller LAUNDRIX-style operational suite (inventory, buyer portals, multi-factory analytics) as the product matures.
Per-factory monthly subscription (tiered by number of active workers/lines).
Free tier for a single production line, to let small factories try it risk-free.
Optional paid add-on: compliance report exports formatted for buyer audits (BSCI/WRAP-style documentation).

This document is a build plan, not a rigid spec — if a module is taking longer than budgeted, cut scope inside that module (drop a field, skip an edge case, simplify the UI) before cutting an entire module. The Grievance module (Part 5) and a working end-to-end Bundle scan flow (Part 6) are the two pieces that must work well for a strong hackathon submission; everything else is depth on top of that foundation.
